thread:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — Elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts on dedicated-cluster apogee-east-2 (customer: Apogee Systems). Paging maya (oncall) and infra team.
maya (oncall): I'm on it. seeing a jump in 502/504s from the gateway at ~12:03 UTC. Grafana shows a spike in p50->p95 and a KV eviction increase.
ton y: is this limited to Apogee or cluster-wide?
kevin: looks customer-specific — traffic from apogee tenant shows error rate ~28% over last 5m, others normal.
samir: noisy neighbor suspected; QPS for apogee ML worker pods spiked, causing KV cache thrashing and backend timeouts.
julia-support: Apogee-ops contacted us: "we're seeing 5xx on production — blocks page loads" — customer impact: live users affected, some payments endpoints timing out.
maya (oncall): steps: 1) confirm eviction logs 2) check GPU / pod saturation 3) apply immediate mitigation (throttle/route/fallback)
infra-bot: KV cache eviction rate: 1.1k evictions/min (baseline 20). Node GPU util: 95% on nodes apogee-rt-02 and apogee-rt-03. Network egress normal.
maya (oncall): running kubectl top pods -n dedicated-apogee --selector=tenant=apogee
--- pasted command output ---
kevin: output shows two pods with 99% CPU and 14GB MEM, num_workers=8 each. Model batch queue lengths at 300+.
samir: looks like a batch amplification event from a new client rollout? any sudden traffic pattern change?
apogee-ops: we deployed a version at 11:58 UTC that increased concurrent prompt fanout, yes. Rolling back now.
maya (oncall): immediate mitigation: 1) apply per-tenant concurrency cap in the gateway 2) route new requests to apogee-fallback pool (quantized model variant) 3) scale up dedicated pool if autoscaling allowed
kevin: setting concurrency cap to 40 for Apogee in gateway config now — patching with curl to control plane API:
```
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/tenants/apogee/config \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP' \
  -d '{"max_concurrency":40}'
```
infra-bot: gateway config change applied, live.
samir: creating a routing rule to pin Apogee to apogee-fallback pool with quantized-4bit-variant to reduce memory pressure:
```
PATCH /routing/policies/apogee
body: {"route_to":"apogee-fallback","duration":"15m","reason":"emergency mitigation - noisy neighbor"}
```
maya (oncall): scaling dedicated pool +2 nodes now (requested via autoscaler). ETA ~90s for new nodes to register.
kevin: adding temporary model-level throttles on the serving runtime: per-request token limit 512 and max_batch_size 64.
julia-support: Apogee-ops confirms rollback started at 12:08 UTC. We'll keep them updated.
apogee-ops: rollback accepted, estimated traffic drop in 2m.
15s later...
infra-bot: new nodes registered: apogee-rt-04, apogee-rt-05. KV eviction rate dropping to 400/min, error rate falling to 12%.
maya (oncall): good. continue monitoring. set on-call handoff to tony in 20m if still ongoing.
kevin: error rate now 6% and trending down. Latency p95 improved from 1.9s to 850ms.
samir: I recommend creating automatic tenant backpressure: if KV eviction > 500/min then apply transient cap. I'll file a follow-up ticket.
julia-support: Customer update: "we saw errors earlier but rollback helped. Thanks for the quick response."
apogee-ops: Appreciated, will wait for full stabilization before resuming rollout.
maya (oncall): postmortem actions: - enforce per-tenant rollout circuit breaker - add a capacity guard for large fanouts - surface tenant throttling in Console - add an alert for KV eviction > 200/min on dedicated clusters.
kevin: will add telemetry for batch queue length and per-tenant memory pressure.
samir: filing infra ticket INF-2872 for capacity planning and permanent routing fallback option.
infra-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring.
maya (oncall): handing over to tony for the monitoring period. Tony, watch for regression in next 30m and coordinate with support for any customer follow-ups.
tony: taking over. thanks team. :thumbsup:
End of thread.
